candidates.statement: This guidance is intended to assist applicants of human prescription drug and biological 18 products 2 in determining the appropriate placement and content of drug interaction (DI) 19 information in labeling as described in the regulations for the content and format of labeling for 20 human prescription drug and biological products. 3 , 4 The purpose of this guidance is to provide 21 recommendations to help ensure that appropriate DI information is consistently placed in the 22 proper sections and subsections within labeling so that the information is clear and accessible to 23 health care practitioners (HCPs) and includes content that guides the safe and effective use of the 24 drug. Applicants should follow the recommendations in this guidance when developing this 25 section of labeling for a new drug submitted to the FDA under a new drug application under 26 section 505(b) of the FD&C Act or a biologics license application under section 351(a) of the 27

candidates.statement: Information about clinically significant DIs should be communicated in the DRUG 111 INTERACTIONS section in a manner that is understandable and clinically informative to HCPs, 112 including those with limited clinical pharmacology expertise. Descriptions of DIs should 113 generally contain information presented in the following order to promote consistency, as 114 applicable: (1) instructions for preventing or managing the clinically significant DIs, (2) 115 mechanisms of the clinically significant DIs, and (3) clinical effects of the clinically significant 116 DIs. This labeling approach prioritizes the information that is most actionable and may impact 117

Instructions to prevent or manage clinically significant DIs in the DRUG INTERACTIONS 122 section must be accurate, 23 specific, and practical 24 and should be actionable for the HCP. For 123 example, a prevention or management recommendation for a clinically significant DI of the 124 subject drug with warfarin that describes a specific change in the frequency or timing of 125 international normalized ratio (INR) monitoring is more informative for HCPs than a non- 126 specific recommendation such as “monitor INR” that reflects standard clinical practice for 127 patients taking warfarin. Applicants should use specific statements rather than vague or 128 ambiguous statements (e.g., “avoid concomitant use” is preferred over “use with caution,” 129 “reduce dosage” is preferred over “adjust dosage”) and use active voice instead of passive voice. 130

candidates.statement: A typical approach to including PK-based DIs in this section is to incorporate such information 431 into one of two subsections: 7.1 Effects of Other Drugs on DRUG-X or 7.2 Effects of DRUG- 432 X on Other Drugs . For complex PK-based DI scenarios (e.g., DRUG-X is affected by and has 433 an effect on the concomitant drug), DI information should be included under both subsections 434 (e.g., 7.1 Effects of Other Drugs on DRUG-X and 7.2 Effects of DRUG-X on Other Drugs ) in 435 order to accurately describe both DIs. PD-related DIs should generally be presented in separate 436 subsection(s) with a title specific to the interacting drug or drug interacting class, as applicable. 437 If there are clinically significant DIs with the subject drug that combine two or more 438 mechanisms, the FDA recommends that the heading that describes such information in the 439 DRUG INTERACTIONS section include all the mechanisms (e.g., Combined P-gp and 440 Moderate CYP3A Inhibitors). This approach should also be used for scenarios involving one or 441 more DI mechanisms in a specific population (e.g., Combined P-gp and Moderate CYP3A 442 Inhibitors in Patients with Renal Impairment). 443
